name: Linear Maps and Proof
strandNote: Not needed to be hired. Quant researcher at firms that hire maths PhDs; reading proofs in papers.
description: Rebuild linear algebra from its axioms and prove the theorems you have been using.

lessonNames.l8-maps-as-matrices: A map as a matrix in a basis

lessonObjectives.l1-axioms: Check the vector space axioms for lists, polynomials and functions.
lessonObjectives.l2-subspaces-and-sums: Prove a subset is a subspace, and tell a sum from a direct sum.
lessonObjectives.l3-span-and-independence: Prove that an independent list is never longer than a spanning list.
lessonObjectives.l4-bases-and-dimension: Prove that every basis has the same length, and extend an independent list to a basis.
lessonObjectives.l5-linear-maps: Prove a map is linear, and show that a linear map is fixed by what it does to a basis.
lessonObjectives.l6-kernel-and-image: Prove that the kernel and image are subspaces, and that a map is one-to-one exactly when its kernel is zero.
lessonObjectives.l7-rank-nullity: Prove the rank-nullity theorem and use it to count solutions.
lessonObjectives.l8-maps-as-matrices: Write a linear map as a matrix in chosen bases, and change basis.
lessonObjectives.l9-invertible-and-isomorphic: Prove that two finite-dimensional spaces are isomorphic exactly when they have the same dimension.
lessonObjectives.l10-dual-space: Build the dual basis, and link the dual map to the transpose.
lessonObjectives.l11-inner-products: Check the inner product axioms, including covariance as an inner product on returns.
lessonObjectives.l12-cauchy-schwarz: Prove the Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities, and see why a correlation lies between $-1$ and $1$.
lessonObjectives.l13-gram-schmidt-proved: Prove that Gram-Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis with the same span.
lessonObjectives.l14-orthogonal-complements: Prove that a space splits as a subspace plus its orthogonal complement, and that projection minimises distance.
lessonObjectives.l15-eigenvalues-exist: Prove that every operator on a complex finite-dimensional space has an eigenvalue.
lessonObjectives.l16-self-adjoint: Prove that a self-adjoint operator has real eigenvalues and perpendicular eigenvectors.
lessonObjectives.l17-spectral-theorem: Prove the spectral theorem for symmetric matrices without notes.
lessonObjectives.l18-generalised-eigenvectors: Find generalised eigenvectors when an operator has too few eigenvectors.
lessonObjectives.l19-jordan-form: Find the Jordan form of a small matrix and read its eigenvalues’ multiplicities from it.
